description.narrative: Det övergripande målet: att bidra till att stärka Ukrainas övervakning av smittsamma sjukdomar, testkapacitet och folkhälsosäkerhet. Förslaget innehåller tre insatser: 1)Säkerställa säker blodförsörjning med 100 % testtäckning för hiv, hepatit B och C (HBV, HCV) och syfilis på viktiga blodinrättningar 2)Implementera robusta protokoll för hantering av kylkedjan för att förhindra vaccinnedbrytning och upprätthålla immuniseringsprogrammets säkerhet och effektivitet 3)Bygga institutionell kapacitet genom evidensbaserade utbildningsprogram som förbättrar laboratoriestandarder, övervakningsprotokoll och ledarskapskapacitet inom Ukrainas folkhälsocenter och regionala centra för förebyggande och kontroll av sjukdomar (rCDC) och blodcentraler/blodbankar.

The overall goal: to contribute to strengthening of Ukraine's communicable diseases surveillance, testing capacity and the public health security. The proposal includes three interventions: 1)Ensuring safe blood supply with 100% testing coverage for HIV, Hepatitis B and C (HBV, HCV) and Syphilis across key blood establishments 2)Implementing robust cold chain management protocols to prevent vaccine degradation and maintain immunization programme safety and effectiveness 3)Building institutional capacity through evidence-based training programmes that enhance laboratory standards, surveillance protocols, and leadership capabilities within the Ukrainian Public Health Center and Regional Centers for Diseases Prevention and Control (rCDCs), and Blood Centers.

To contribute to strengthen Ukraine's communicable diseases surveillance, testing capacity and the public health security in Ukraine.
Strategic interventions:
1. Ensuring safe blood supply with 100% testing coverage for HIV, Hepatitis B and C (HBV, HCV) and Syphilis across key blood establishments
2. Implementing robust cold chain management protocols to prevent vaccine degradation and maintain immunization programme safety and effectiveness
3. Building institutional capacity through evidence-based training programmes that enhance laboratory standards, surveillance protocols, and leadership capabilities within the Ukrainian Public Health Center and Regional Centers for Diseases Prevention and Control (rCDCs), and Blood Centers.

Reporting October 2025 to March 2026.
Continued attacks (Ukraine recorded 28% increased attacks on health care assists in the first quarter of 2026) on and sustained pressures on health services keep trauma care needs high, which in turn increased demand for safe blood and uninterrupted screening to prevent transfusion-transmissible infections. At the same time, disruptions to energy and logistics systems heighten the risk of cold chain failures, making this contribution very relevant.
This supported allowed WHO Ukraine to protect two life lines that the war keeps compromising: 1) the safety of blood transfusion, and 2) the protection of vaccine supply chain. In parallel, WHO Ukraine strengthened the human capacity of Ukraine's public health system, especially laboratory staff and public health leaders, so they can detect threats earlier, work safer, and sustain quality under pressure.
WHO converted Sida's investment into three (3) main practical results: 1) WHO delivered targeted blood safety supplies to prevent interruptions in screening and to reduce the risk of transfusion- transmissible infections (TTIs)
2) WHO helped Ukraine's immunization programme prevent "invisible losses" of vaccine potency by moving from review to practical field - oriented standard operating procedures (SOPs) and by addressing urgent infrastructure risks at the national vaccine warehouse.
3) WHO strengthened quality and bio-safety practices in laboratories through hands-on trainings, on-line learning, mentorship and accreditation-readiness assessments that translate into more reliable results and safer working conditions.
These results contributed directly to the project goal: strengthening communicable disease surveillance and testing capacity and, through that , public health security in Ukraine.
More specific results
- 23 blood centres received blood containers to sustain blood collection and processing.
- 1 blood establishment received HIV syphilis and anti HCV testing supplies and two months contingency stock.
- 1 ELISA equipment set was procured for the National Service Reference Laboratory in Vinnytsia oblast
- 1 national standard operation procedure (SOP) on Temperature Recording and management of Temperature Excursion developed.
- Major vaccine potency loss prevented by addressing cold chain risk at the national vaccine warehouse, protecting over 5 million doses from freezing.
- 3 blood establishment assessments and capacity building activities, including two webinars reaching over 300 participants (information on disaggregation of male and females exist in annex- should be noted that over 90% of the professional in the lab are females).
